title: Caerlon: turnbased Space Exploration
author: Powerful_Hour_5584
selftext:
I’m a solo dev, and Caelorn is a space strategy game inspired by the PBEM classics like VGA Planets. Every empire writes its orders in secret, and when the deadline passes, the host resolves all turns at once. It runs in the browser at one turn a day, so it fits around real life.

A few things I cared about:

•	⁠True fog of war. The server decides what you see. Distant worlds show as last observed, never live.  
•	⁠Open formulas. Mining, growth, fuel and production follow documented, deterministic rules. No hidden dice, and every turn can be replayed exactly.  
•	⁠Balanced maps. Every map, including player-created ones, has to pass a fairness check.  
•	⁠Stable rules. If a new ruleset is published mid-game, running games keep the ruleset they started with.  
•	⁠Fair AI. AI opponents fill empty seats and see only what a human in their place would.

Before inviting anyone, I ran over 20,000 simulated games between AI opponents to tune the balance. But bots only find the exploits I taught them to look for, and human players are far better at breaking things. The game is in active development and the balance is provisional, which is exactly why I need you: play, try to break it, and tell me what felt wrong.

Up to 8 players per game · one turn per day · free · browser, nothing to install
